trust_decision.summary: Whether a response that renders notebook-derived (attacker-authorable) HTML on the server origin is confined to an opaque origin via a CSP 'sandbox allow-scripts' directive; decided per handler in its content_security_policy property, which nbconvert handlers do not override at the pinned commit (files handlers do).

landing_point.why: Summary names NbconvertFileHandler / NbconvertPostHandler directly; both live in this one file, and the existing sandbox pattern in jupyter_server/files/handlers.py:34-39 is the obvious template.

fix_sites.entry_point: ServerWebApplication settings dict (fix.diff:74) feeding self.settings for the handlers
new traitlet ServerApp.nbconvert_csp_sandbox (fix.diff:82-89), config file / CLI

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: Both handler fixes sit in jupyter_server/nbconvert/handlers.py next to each other; the serverapp.py changes are only a config toggle (fix.diff:74, fix.diff:82-89), not a second route into the sink.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: For the O8 kernelspec route: 'kernelspec resources are admin-installed kernel logos, not notebook content, and the advisory is about nbconvert rendering', so it is a neighbouring feature.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: If the fix adds sandbox to the shared base CSP (AuthenticatedHandler/JupyterHandler), every same-origin UI page (main, login, extension pages) loses its origin, so cookies, XSRF, and frontend JS break. Also nbconvert_csp_sandbox=False must leave the CSP without sandbox, and a user-supplied CSP from settings['headers'] is still the base.

O6_input_shapes: notebook loaded from contents manager by path (GET)
notebook model posted as JSON body (POST)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: GET /kernelspecs/<kernel>/<path> serves kernelspec resource files (any extension, mimetype guessed, so .html/.svg render) on the server origin. It is a plain JupyterHandler with no sandbox in its CSP, on both the disk branch and the KSM get_kernel_spec_resource branch.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Kernelspec resources are logos installed by kernel packages/admins, not notebook output; a different feature from nbconvert.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a 'raw' view mode that writes rendered HTML directly instead of embedding /files in the sandboxed iframe (jupyter_server/templates/view.html:31)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A maintainer adding a no-iframe preview would reuse JupyterHandler and forget the CSP override, the same omission nbconvert made.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an export/preview endpoint that serves one member of the respond_zip resources inline (text/html) instead of as an attachment
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The zip helper already holds resource outputs; serving a selected one inline is a plausible convenience feature with no handler-level CSP.

O9_family: XSS via missing CSP sandbox on user-content rendering responses (CWE-79/CWE-1021)

O10_build.toolchain: pip / hatch, pytest with pytest-jupyter (jp_fetch, jp_server_config fixtures); nbconvert must be installed
O10_build.project_tests: tests/nbconvert/test_handlers.py (fix adds test_csp_file_handler / test_csp_post_handler at fix.diff:104-136), tests/test_files.py, kernelspec resource tests under tests/

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Copy the files/handlers.py content_security_policy override into NbconvertFileHandler only (the GET path in the report), missing the POST handler and the config toggle.

out_of_scope_notes: GatewayResourceHandler (jupyter_server/gateway/handlers.py:287-305) serves remote-gateway kernelspec resources with a guessed mimetype, but as an APIHandler it inherits default-src 'none' (jupyter_server/base/handlers.py:791-799), so scripts are already blocked; not an uncovered route.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell used); tiny_repo flag not assessed.
present_in_latest for the kernelspec route is unknown (no latest release given).

Weak host overall: the fix is two identical 5-line property overrides in one file. Both handlers are named in the summary, so they fall together (a WHERE-type fix with little HOW-type room). The only lever is the kernelspec route, and it is also WHERE-type.
Fairness: hidden tests pinning the exact trait name nbconvert_csp_sandbox would need that name stated in the report.
Whether a non-admin can write kernelspec resource dirs (e.g. ~/.local/share/jupyter/kernels inside root_dir) was not checked; this affects whether the O8 route is attacker-reachable.
